understanding: The task is to finalize OKO VLM Chapter 5 by refactoring its codebase into atomic, modular components, conducting an honest demonstration that reflects the true state of the code, and achieving formal stakeholder acceptance. This is the final iteration, so all work must be complete, tests must pass, and the demo must be transparent about any limitations.
summary: Complete final refactoring of OKO VLM Chapter 5 into atomic modules, execute a truthful demo showing real capabilities and limitations, obtain formal sign-off, and deliver a status report confirming readiness. All existing tests pass, coding standards are met, and the modular structure is verified.

decision_atoms.statement: Decompose Chapter 5 codebase into atomic modules based on single-responsibility principle.
decision_atoms.reason: Atomic modules improve maintainability, testability, and align with the 'by atoms' constraint.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Increased number of files and inter-module dependencies may complicate initial navigation, but long-term clarity is gained.

decision_atoms.statement: Conduct an honest demo using the refactored code without any mockups or hidden fallbacks.
decision_atoms.reason: The constraint explicitly requires the demo to reflect the true state of the code to build trust and enable valid acceptance.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Exposing real limitations might raise stakeholder concerns, but honesty prevents future disputes and ensures genuine acceptance.

decision_atoms.statement: Run all existing automated tests after refactoring and fix any regressions before demo.
decision_atoms.reason: Success test requires all tests to pass; regressions would indicate broken modularization.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Time spent fixing regressions delays demo, but skipping it risks formal acceptance failure.

decision_atoms.statement: Formally document the modular architecture and demo results for stakeholder acceptance.
decision_atoms.reason: Formal acceptance requires evidence of completed work and adherence to constraints.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Documentation overhead increases effort, but without it acceptance cannot be objectively verified.

assumptions: OKO VLM Chapter 5 codebase is accessible and can be modified.
Existing automated tests cover core functionality of Chapter 5.
Stakeholders are available for the demo and acceptance process.
Atomic modularization means separating concerns into distinct, independently testable components (functions, classes, or files).
The current code state is functional but not yet modularized.

risks.risk: Refactoring introduces regressions not caught by existing tests.
risks.mitigation: Expand test coverage before refactoring; perform incremental refactoring with continuous integration checks.

risks.risk: Stakeholders reject the demo due to exposed limitations.
risks.mitigation: Set expectations beforehand; frame limitations as known scope boundaries of Chapter 5 and propose future chapters.

risks.risk: Modular boundaries are incorrectly drawn, causing tight coupling.
risks.mitigation: Review modular design with peers before implementation; use dependency inversion where appropriate.

risks.risk: Time constraints prevent full modularization before deadline.
risks.mitigation: Prioritize core modules; if needed, propose a phased acceptance with minimal viable modularization first.

minimal_version: Refactor core Chapter 5 logic into 3-5 atomic modules, ensure all tests pass, perform honest demo with basic documentation, obtain conditional acceptance with minor punch-list items.
advanced_version: Full atomic decomposition with clear interface contracts, comprehensive test suite including integration tests, interactive demo with live Q&A, detailed architecture document, and unconditional formal acceptance.
